reasoning_checks: Same-horizon decimal simple total returns and beginning-wealth budget; no interim trading, fees, taxes or observed market data. Physical sign probabilities are not pricing probabilities.
Main law has sixteen equiprobable states and SPD covariance .01*11T + diag(.01,.04,.09); independent loading-Gram and projected-state moments agree.
GMV sufficiency follows orthogonal budget perturbations; target sufficiency follows both equality constraints. Delta positivity requires nonconstant means, whereas SPD alone suffices for GMV.
Upper/lower branch distinction is proved using reflected means; unrestricted target portfolios remain feasible because shorting is expressly allowed.
Safe weight is 1-sum(x), not silently excluded. Total portfolio moments differ from fully invested risky fund moments. Positive, zero, negative and all-zero-premium cases are separately checked.

Sharpe maximization uses its signed ratio. A negative risky-direction normalizer cannot be called the same positive-premium fully invested fund, even though the unrestricted cash/risky optimum exists.

Long-only scalar curve and KKT signs independently verify the endpoint optimum. Clipping does not preserve the target. Capped inequality solution has correct multiplier signs and a global feasible-direction certificate.

Mean-variance is stipulated for bounded state laws. Normal/exponential equivalence is conditional and quadratic utility is not silently replaced by a constant-gamma mean-variance ranking. Equal moments do not determine the discrete exponential utility comparison.
Shrinkage rules are computed from forecast inputs only. All audit values use one separately specified synthetic population and are not optimized fitted values from different models.

The alternate population has the raw forecast moments as truth; completing the square gives loss gamma*(.04-.0396)*(d-dstar)^2, proving that the shrinkage improvement in the disclosed audit law is not universal.

Identity shrinkage can create estimated curvature but cannot discover genuine risk in a duplicate-asset zero-risk direction. Redundancy and short-sample singularity require different modeling judgments.
Every exercise has sufficient data and previously taught methods. The empirical-design response provides evaluation criteria rather than claiming a unique opinion or real forecasting result.
